articles.title: GDScript: The Good, Bad, and Ugly Parts
articles.summary: GDScript is a high-level language designed specifically for game logic implementation in video games, offering features such as native Vector2 and Vector3 types, integer and floating-point number distinction, a match statement, and support for packed arrays. Its tightly coupled nature with the Godot engine enables developers to write node classes with editor panels for easy configuration, and its treatment of signals as a first-class concept is useful for game programming. The language also has no garbage collector, which is unique among high-level languages, although its performance characteristics are somewhat unpredictable.

articles.title: "Do You Still Read the Code?"
articles.summary: The practice of reading code is evolving, with some developers opting for AI-powered tools to streamline their development process. However, this shift may not be as seamless as it seems, as it can lead to a loss of understanding and maintenance of the codebase. Accelerators, which use AI to translate code into a more maintainable form, are one approach, but they require discipline and attention to detail to ensure the generated code is accurate and effective. Vibecoders, on the other hand, delegate implementation to AI, expecting language models to abstract away technical details, but this may not be the future of software development.

articles.title: Why is the x86 undefined instruction called ud2? Why 2?
articles.summary: The x86 undefined instruction called ud2 is an architecturally undefined instruction that raises an invalid opcode exception when executed, guaranteeing a crash if the program attempts to reach it. This instruction is not named ud1 but is instead called ud2 due to its similar properties and the fact that it was the first to reliably raise an invalid opcode exception. The existence of ud2 is a result of the 0F FF and 0F B9 sequences, which were both found to cause invalid opcode exceptions, and the subsequent attempts to define a new instruction or modify the existing one.
